subject: Plain-language DPA blurb + console data-residency toggle
messages:
From: Maria Ortiz <maria.ortiz@acmecloud.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Legal <legal@acmecloud.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask: DPA short blurb + console toggle behavior

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked how Redwood's routing and caching cut tail latency. Legal and product want two small things before we proceed to procurement: a one-paragraph, plain-language DPA blurb we can publish to our privacy page (and link in our procurement portal), and a short explanation of how the console "data residency" toggle behaves when customers change regions.

Specifically:
- Can you give us a 2–3 sentence copy that explains what data is processed in-hosted mode vs. what stays in-customer control under Dedicated/Private? We need it non-legal, customer-facing.
- If a customer flips the console residence toggle (e.g., from us-west to eu-central), what happens to in-flight requests, archived logs, and subprocessor transfers? We need the operational behavior and any expected timeline for data movement.

Attachments: I attached Acme's procurement checklist and the legal team's baseline DPA language for reference.

Goal: get something legal is comfortable with and a short UI help text for the toggle by EOD Friday.

Best,
Maria Ortiz
Head of Platform Compliance
Acme Cloud

Attachments: procurement_checklist.pdf (pdf), legal_dpa_baseline.pdf (pdf)

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Maria Ortiz <maria.ortiz@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: DPA short blurb + console toggle behavior

Maria — thanks, I can take point on this and loop in Legal for sign-off. High level answers below; attaching a plain-language DPA blurb draft and a couple console mock screenshots for the help tooltip.

Plain-language blurb (draft, 2 sentences):
"Redwood Inference processes customer requests on behalf of customers and does not use customer content to train models. For teams using the hosted API, request content and short-term inference caches are processed in the region selected; for Dedicated or Private deployments, customer data remains within your reserved capacity and network boundary unless you explicitly authorize a transfer."

Console toggle behavior (short):
- In-flight requests: remain served by the existing runtime in the older region until completion; new requests after the switch are routed to the new region.
- Archived logs & audit traces: we do not migrate historical logs automatically. If you request migration we run a controlled transfer (DocuSign + approval) and provide an ETA — typically 48–72 hours depending on volume.
- Subprocessor transfers: changing the region does not add new subprocessors by default; any move that requires a new data center provider will be surfaced in the subprocessor list and require notification/consent per the DPA.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly: quick legal review of the blurb and confirm we can include the migration ETA.
2) Laura: product to finalize the help text and small console tooltip (see attached screenshots) and confirm exact copy length.
3) Maria: confirm Acme is comfortable with the migration window and whether they want automatic archival migration for compliance audits.

I'll shepherd the sign-off. Attaching: DPA_plain_language_draft_v2.docx, console_ui_screenshots.zip

—Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_plain_language_draft_v2.docx (docx), console_ui_screenshots.zip (zip)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Maria Ortiz <maria.ortiz@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: DPA short blurb + console toggle behavior

Thanks Rohan — I reviewed and made two small edits to the blurb for clarity (attached as tracked changes in the docx). Key clarifications:
- Remove the phrase "unless you explicitly authorize a transfer" and replace with "unless a customer requests data migration or selects a deployment option that includes data movement." That avoids implying any silent transfers.
- Add one clause: "Redwood maintains a published subprocessor list and will notify customers of any changes at least 30 days before processors begin handling customer content."

On migration ETA: 48–72 hours is reasonable operationally, but for the DPA we should say "typical range 48–96 hours depending on dataset size and export approvals." Keeps expectations conservative.

Maria — one small ask from Legal: can Acme confirm whether their procurement team requires automatic migration of archived logs as part of the contract, or whether they prefer manual request per-incident? That changes how we phrase the UI copy — automatic migrations imply a background job and different controls.

Laura, product: please take Rohan's UI screenshots and produce a 2-line tooltip + 1-sentence help center blurb. I'll sign off after the final wording.

Kimberly Park
Counsel, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_plain_language_draft_v2_kp_edits.docx (docx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maria Ortiz <maria.ortiz@acmecloud.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask: DPA short blurb + console toggle behavior

Maria — attaching the UI copy per Kimberly's edits. Proposed help tooltip (shown in console next to "Data residency"):

Tooltip (2 lines):
"Select where requests are processed. New requests are routed to the chosen region; in-flight requests complete in the previous region."

Help center blurb (1 sentence):
"Switching regions routes new traffic to the selected data center; historic logs are not moved automatically — contact support to request a controlled export and migration (typical completion 48–96 hours). Changes that require new subprocessors will be shown in the published subprocessor list and notified 30 days in advance."

Maria — can you confirm whether Acme wants the console to show an explicit "migrate historical logs" checkbox when changing residency, or prefer that migration requests go through procurement/legal? We can implement either but CTA and wording differ.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Console
Redwood Inference

Attachment: data_residency_tooltip_preview.png (png)
